**IE-494 · Big Data Processing · Autumn 2026** Instructor: PM Jat (`pm_jat@dau.ac.in`) Student: Aditya Vaish · ID `202401401` Submitted: **Constraint:** Spark **RDD API only**. No DataFrames, Datasets, or Spark SQL. --- ## Assignment Implement **basic YAFIM** (Yet Another Frequent Itemset Mining) on Spark RDDs: - Paper Algorithm 2 — frequent 1-itemsets - Paper Algorithm 3 — frequent k-itemsets for k ≥ 2 (apriori-gen + broadcast hash tree + `subset()`) - Mine the FIMI `retail.dat` dataset ([http://fimi.uantwerpen.be/data/retail.dat](http://fimi.uantwerpen.be/data/retail.dat)) with `minSupport = 1000` **Citation:** Hongjian Qiu, Rong Gu, Chunfeng Yuan, Yihua Huang, *YAFIM: A Parallel Frequent Itemset Mining Algorithm with Spark*, IEEE International Parallel & Distributed Processing Symposium Workshops (**IPDPSW 2014**). ## Dataset `retail.dat` is a market-basket file from the FIMI repository: one transaction per line, **space-separated integer item IDs**.
**property** **value**
transactions (baskets) 88,162
encoding space-separated item IDs, one basket per line
minSupport 1000
relative support 1000 / 88162 ≈ 1.13%
Spark master `local[*]` (Spark 4.2.0, `spark-core_2.13`, Java 17)
API Java RDD only — no DataFrame / Dataset / Spark SQL
A tiny `data/toy.dat` (5 baskets) is used as a sanity check with `minSupport = 3`. --- ## Algorithm YAFIM is Apriori on Spark RDDs. The transaction RDD is **parsed once, cached**, and reused for every pass. ### Phase I — Algorithm 2 (frequent 1-itemsets) 1. `flatMap` each cached transaction to `(item, 1)` pairs. 2. `reduceByKey` to support counts. 3. Keep items with count ≥ `minSupport`. That list is `L1`. ### Phase II — Algorithm 3 (k ≥ 2) For k = 2, 3, … until `Ck` or `Lk` is empty: 1. **apriori-gen:** self-join frequent (k−1)-itemsets on a shared (k−2)-prefix, then prune any k-candidate whose (k−1)-subsets are not all frequent. 2. Build an in-memory **hash tree** of `Ck` (branch factor 11, leaf split after 4 candidates) and **broadcast** it. 3. Each partition runs `subset()` / `HashTree.findCandidates` on every cached transaction: walk the tree by hashing successive items, and at leaves test `containsAll`. 4. `flatMap` matching candidates to `(key, 1)`, `reduceByKey`, keep counts ≥ `minSupport` → `Lk`. `SparkContext.collect()` returns an unmodifiable list, so results are copied into `new ArrayList<>(...)` before `List.sort`. ### Hash-tree support counting (bug fix) Hashing two different items into the same bucket can visit a leaf **more than once** for the same transaction. Without dedupe, the same candidate was emitted multiple times per basket, which **inflated support**. Example before the fix: pair `39,48` counted **75856** (YAFIM) vs **29142** (lab3 MR-Apriori), and `|L2|` was **227** instead of **49**. `findCandidates` now records keys in a `LinkedHashSet` and returns each candidate **once** per transaction. After the fix, YAFIM matches lab3 on every itemset key and count. --- ## How to run From `lab5/`. `mvn exec:java` does **not** recompile unless you also `package` / `compile`. ```bash cd lab5 bash run_all.sh ``` Equivalent Maven commands: ```bash cd lab5 mvn -DskipTests package # retail.dat, minSupport=1000 mvn exec:java \ -Dexec.mainClass=pmj.bdp.spark.lab5.Yafim \ -Dexec.args="$(pwd)/data/retail.dat 1000 $(pwd)/output/yafim" # toy sanity check, minSupport=3 mvn exec:java \ -Dexec.mainClass=pmj.bdp.spark.lab5.Yafim \ -Dexec.args="$(pwd)/data/toy.dat 3 $(pwd)/output/toy" ``` Outputs: `output/yafim/L1.txt` … `L4.txt` and `frequent-itemsets.txt` (tab-separated `itemset\tsupport`). --- ## Evaluation ### Toy sanity check (`toy.dat`, minSupport = 3) 5 transactions. Expected: L1 = items 1, 2, 3; three frequent pairs; L3 empty (the triple 1,2,3 has support 2).

Spark RDD only.
Yafim.java (full) ```java package pmj.bdp.spark.lab5; import java.io.BufferedWriter; import java.io.IOException; import java.nio.file.Files; import java.nio.file.Path; import java.util.ArrayList; import java.util.Comparator; import java.util.List; import org.apache.spark.api.java.JavaPairRDD; import org.apache.spark.api.java.JavaRDD; import org.apache.spark.api.java.JavaSparkContext; import org.apache.spark.broadcast.Broadcast; import scala.Tuple2; /** * YAFIM — Yet Another Frequent Itemset Mining * (Qiu, Gu, Yuan, Huang; IEEE IPDPSW 2014). * * Spark RDD only (no DataFrame / SQL). Two phases from the paper: * Algo-2 frequent 1-itemsets L1 (flatMap + reduceByKey + minsup filter) * Algo-3 frequent k-itemsets, k ≥ 2 (apriori-gen, broadcast hash tree, * subset() on each cached transaction, reduceByKey) * * Usage: Yafim <transactions> [minSupport] [outputDir] * Defaults: minSupport=1000, outputDir=output/yafim */ public class Yafim { public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException { if (args.length < 1) { System.err.println("Usage: Yafim [minSupport] [outputDir]"); System.exit(1); } String input = args[0]; int minSupport = args.length > 1 ? Integer.parseInt(args[1]) : 1000; Path outDir = Path.of(args.length > 2 ? args[2] : "output/yafim"); JavaSparkContext sc = SparkUtil.localContext("Lab5 YAFIM"); try { run(sc, input, minSupport, outDir); } finally { sc.stop(); sc.close(); } } static void run(JavaSparkContext sc, String input, int minSupport, Path outDir) throws IOException { Files.createDirectories(outDir); JavaRDD transactions = sc.textFile(input) .map(Itemset::parseTransaction) .filter(t -> t.length > 0) .cache(); long n = transactions.count(); System.out.println("transactions = " + n); System.out.println("minSupport = " + minSupport + " (" + String.format("%.4f", minSupport / (double) n) + " of n)"); List> allFrequent = new ArrayList<>(); // ---- Algo-2: Phase I, frequent 1-itemsets ---- System.out.println(); System.out.println("======== YAFIM Algo-2 L1 ========"); List> l1kv = algo2Frequent1(transactions, minSupport); List lk = keysToItemsets(l1kv); System.out.println("|L1| = " + lk.size()); writeLevel(outDir.resolve("L1.txt"), l1kv); allFrequent.addAll(l1kv); // ---- Algo-3: Phase II, k >= 2 ---- for (int k = 2; ; k++) { System.out.println(); System.out.println("======== YAFIM Algo-3 L" + k + " ========"); List ck = Itemset.generateCandidates(lk); System.out.println("|C" + k + "| = " + ck.size()); if (ck.isEmpty()) { break; } List> lkkv = algo3FrequentK(sc, transactions, ck, minSupport); lk = keysToItemsets(lkkv); System.out.println("|L" + k + "| = " + lk.size()); if (lk.isEmpty()) { break; } writeLevel(outDir.resolve("L" + k + ".txt"), lkkv); allFrequent.addAll(lkkv); } Path combined = outDir.resolve("frequent-itemsets.txt"); writeLevel(combined, allFrequent); System.out.println(); System.out.println("Wrote " + allFrequent.size() + " frequent itemsets to " + combined); } /** * Paper Algorithm 2 — Phase I. * Transactions RDD already cached. flatMap items to (item, 1), * reduceByKey, keep counts ≥ minsup. */ static List> algo2Frequent1( JavaRDD transactions, int minSupport) { JavaPairRDD counts = transactions .flatMapToPair(t -> { List> out = new ArrayList<>(t.length); for (int item : t) { out.add(new Tuple2<>(item, 1)); } return out.iterator(); }) .reduceByKey(Integer::sum) .filter(kv -> kv._2 >= minSupport); List> rows = new ArrayList<>(); for (Tuple2 kv : counts.collect()) { rows.add(new Tuple2<>(Integer.toString(kv._1), kv._2)); } rows.sort(Comparator.comparing(t -> Integer.parseInt(t._1))); return rows; } /** * Paper Algorithm 3 — Phase II for one k. * Build / broadcast a hash tree of Ck, run subset() on each transaction, * reduceByKey, keep counts ≥ minsup. */ static List> algo3FrequentK( JavaSparkContext sc, JavaRDD transactions, List candidates, int minSupport) { Broadcast treeBc = sc.broadcast(new HashTree(candidates)); try { JavaPairRDD counts = transactions .flatMapToPair(t -> { List hits = treeBc.value().findCandidates(t); List> out = new ArrayList<>(hits.size()); for (int[] c : hits) { out.add(new Tuple2<>(Itemset.toKey(c), 1)); } return out.iterator(); }) .reduceByKey(Integer::sum) .filter(kv -> kv._2 >= minSupport); List> rows = new ArrayList<>(counts.collect()); rows.sort(Comparator.comparing(t -> t._1)); return rows; } finally { treeBc.destroy(); } } private static List keysToItemsets(List> rows) { List list = new ArrayList<>(rows.size()); for (Tuple2 row : rows) { list.add(Itemset.parseKey(row._1)); } return list; } private static void writeLevel(Path file, List> rows) throws IOException { try (BufferedWriter w = Files.newBufferedWriter(file)) { for (Tuple2 row : rows) { w.write(row._1); w.write('\t'); w.write(Integer.toString(row._2)); w.newLine(); } } } } ```
HashTree.java (full) ```java package pmj.bdp.spark.lab5; import java.io.Serializable; import java.util.ArrayList; import java.util.LinkedHashSet; import java.util.List; /** * Apriori hash tree used by YAFIM Algo-3 {@code subset()} to find which * candidate k-itemsets a transaction contains (Qiu et al., IPDPSW 2014). * * Interior nodes hash on the next item; leaves store candidates. A leaf * splits once it exceeds {@link #MAX_LEAF} and depth < k. */ public final class HashTree implements Serializable { private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L; private static final int BRANCH = 11; private static final int MAX_LEAF = 4; private final Node root; private final int k; public HashTree(List candidates) { if (candidates == null || candidates.isEmpty()) { throw new IllegalArgumentException("candidates must be non-empty"); } this.k = candidates.get(0).length; this.root = new Node(true); for (int[] c : candidates) { insert(root, c, 0); } } /** * Candidates contained in the (sorted, unique) transaction. * Each candidate is returned at most once: hash collisions can visit the * same leaf via multiple item prefixes, which would otherwise inflate support. */ public List findCandidates(int[] transaction) { LinkedHashSet seen = new LinkedHashSet<>(); List hits = new ArrayList<>(); search(root, transaction, 0, 0, seen, hits); return hits; } private void insert(Node node, int[] itemset, int depth) { if (node.leaf) { node.candidates.add(itemset); if (node.candidates.size() > MAX_LEAF && depth < k) { split(node, depth); } return; } int bucket = bucket(itemset[depth]); if (node.children[bucket] == null) { node.children[bucket] = new Node(true); } insert(node.children[bucket], itemset, depth + 1); } private void split(Node leaf, int depth) { List old = leaf.candidates; leaf.leaf = false; leaf.candidates = null; leaf.children = new Node[BRANCH]; for (int[] c : old) { insert(leaf, c, depth); } } private void search(Node node, int[] t, int depth, int start, LinkedHashSet seen, List hits) { if (node == null) { return; } if (node.leaf) { for (int[] cand : node.candidates) { if (Itemset.containsAll(t, cand) && seen.add(Itemset.toKey(cand))) { hits.add(cand); } } return; } int remaining = k - depth; for (int i = start; i <= t.length - remaining; i++) { Node child = node.children[bucket(t[i])]; if (child != null) { search(child, t, depth + 1, i + 1, seen, hits); } } } private static int bucket(int item) { int m = item % BRANCH; return m < 0 ? m + BRANCH : m; } private static final class Node implements Serializable { private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L; boolean leaf; List candidates; Node[] children; Node(boolean leaf) { this.leaf = leaf; if (leaf) { this.candidates = new ArrayList<>(); } else { this.children = new Node[BRANCH]; } } } } ```
Itemset.java (full) ```java package pmj.bdp.spark.lab5; import java.util.ArrayList; import java.util.Arrays; import java.util.HashSet; import java.util.List; import java.util.Set; /** * Sorted integer itemset helpers (Apriori join + prune). */ public final class Itemset { private Itemset() { } public static int[] parseTransaction(String line) { if (line == null || line.isBlank()) { return new int[0]; } String[] tok = line.trim().split("\\s+"); int[] raw = new int[tok.length]; int n = 0; for (String t : tok) { if (t.isEmpty()) { continue; } raw[n++] = Integer.parseInt(t); } if (n == 0) { return new int[0]; } Arrays.sort(raw, 0, n); int w = 1; for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) { if (raw[i] != raw[w - 1]) { raw[w++] = raw[i]; } } return Arrays.copyOf(raw, w); } public static String toKey(int[] items) { StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder(); for (int i = 0; i < items.length; i++) { if (i > 0) { sb.append(','); } sb.append(items[i]); } return sb.toString(); } public static int[] parseKey(String key) { String[] parts = key.split(","); int[] items = new int[parts.length]; for (int i = 0; i < parts.length; i++) { items[i] = Integer.parseInt(parts[i].trim()); } return items; } /** Both arrays sorted. */ public static boolean containsAll(int[] transaction, int[] candidate) { int i = 0; int j = 0; while (i < transaction.length && j < candidate.length) { if (transaction[i] == candidate[j]) { i++; j++; } else if (transaction[i] < candidate[j]) { i++; } else { return false; } } return j == candidate.length; } /** * Apriori-gen: self-join L_{k-1} then prune candidates whose * (k-1)-subsets are not all frequent. */ public static List generateCandidates(List previous) { List candidates = new ArrayList<>(); if (previous.isEmpty()) { return candidates; } int kMinus1 = previous.get(0).length; Set frequent = new HashSet<>(); for (int[] itemset : previous) { frequent.add(toKey(itemset)); } for (int i = 0; i < previous.size(); i++) { int[] a = previous.get(i); for (int j = i + 1; j < previous.size(); j++) { int[] b = previous.get(j); if (!prefixEqual(a, b, kMinus1 - 1)) { continue; } int lastA = a[kMinus1 - 1]; int lastB = b[kMinus1 - 1]; if (lastA == lastB) { continue; } int[] cand = new int[kMinus1 + 1]; System.arraycopy(a, 0, cand, 0, kMinus1 - 1); if (lastA < lastB) { cand[kMinus1 - 1] = lastA; cand[kMinus1] = lastB; } else { cand[kMinus1 - 1] = lastB; cand[kMinus1] = lastA; } if (allSubsetsFrequent(cand, frequent)) { candidates.add(cand); } } } return candidates; } private static boolean prefixEqual(int[] a, int[] b, int len) { for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) { if (a[i] != b[i]) { return false; } } return true; } private static boolean allSubsetsFrequent(int[] candidate, Set frequent) { int k = candidate.length; int[] subset = new int[k - 1]; for (int drop = 0; drop < k; drop++) { int idx = 0; for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) { if (i != drop) { subset[idx++] = candidate[i]; } } if (!frequent.contains(toKey(subset))) { return false; } } return true; } } ```
